text: IMF staff assesses that persistently high interest rate spreads, hovering around 9 percentage points since September 2008, hamper growth and monetary policy effectiveness. Given market diseconomies of scale, staff views new bank entry as ineffective, recommending instead nonbank financing, digital banking, and creditor legal reforms. Crucially, staff cautions that narrowing spreads without reducing costs poses risks to bank profitability and could cause underpricing of credit risk amid elevated nonperforming loans.
